commands.title: Undo All Changes of the Session

gcode.provider.description: The model provider for chat, review and Cmd-K. Set its key in Geno: Models and Keys, or with `Geno: Set API Key`.

gcode.baseUrl.description: Model Studio's Anthropic-compatible endpoint, which embeds your workspace id and region. Read from your user settings only. Other providers ignore it.

gcode.model.description: The model for chat, review and Cmd-K. Empty uses the provider's default (qwen3.8-flash on Model Studio).

gcode.providers.markdownDescription: Per-provider values that are not secret: a base URL override, an AWS region or profile, a Google Cloud project. Read from your user settings only, so a workspace cannot send your key elsewhere. Keys never go here: set them in **Geno: Models and Keys**, which keeps them in VS Code's secret storage.

gcode.roles.markdownDescription: Which provider and model each helper runs on. Chat runs on `gcode.provider` and `gcode.model`, and Tab on its local llama-server. A role left out keeps Geno's default.

classifier.description: The Auto mode classifier, which judges commands no rule settles. Left out, it runs on the chat provider. A provider without a model runs that provider's classifier default, or its default model.

explore.description: The explore helper, once Geno has one.

enumDescriptions: Ask before every command that is not on the safe list or a saved allow rule. Edits apply without asking; the sandbox and checkpoints cover them.

Run clearly safe commands on its own, any command in the sandbox that no rule flags, and git push to the repository's own branches. A classifier judges the rest, such as downloads, cloud and database CLIs, force pushes, pushes to deploy branches, and any command the agent asks to run outside the sandbox. What the classifier refuses or cannot evaluate goes back to the agent with the reason, and after 3 refusals in a row or 20 in a chat you decide the next one; a classifier that is not set up asks you instead. Geno still asks before deleting the workspace, its .git or a path outside it.
gcode.approvalMode.description: The approval mode new chats start in. The picker in the composer switches the open chat.

gcode.skills.catalogs.markdownDescription: Catalogs of skills and agent definitions to search in Settings, under Skills and agents: the https URL of a `catalog.json` index, or a folder on this machine that holds one. Geno ships with none. An install copies an entry's files as data after checking each one's sha256, and runs nothing.

gcode.browser.enabled.description: Let the agent drive a browser: Chrome through the chrome-devtools-mcp server, with a fresh profile thrown away after each chat. Pages on localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1], *.localhost and *.test open without asking; any other site asks first in Ask, and goes to the classifier in Auto. Chrome starts at the first browser step.

gcode.browser.headless.description: Run the agent's browser without a window. Applies to new chats.

enumDescriptions: Dark glass panes over a soft gradient, with a running rainbow edge on the turn at work and the focused composer.
VS Code's own colors and borders, as the Trail panel had before.
gcode.ui.style.description: How the chat panel looks. High contrast themes always use the native style.

gcode.appearance.tokens.markdownDescription: A theme for the chat panel: Geno's own tokens, such as `--muted` or `--glass-base`, set to CSS values for each kind of color theme, as in `{ "dark": { "--glass-base": "#101418" } }`. A high contrast kind changes only when you name it. Unknown tokens are ignored with a warning, and VS Code's `--vscode-*` variables stay the color theme's. The UI gallery (`pnpm ui`) exports this object.

enumDescriptions: Fold each finished turn's work into one summary line, and show only a running turn's last four steps. Click the line to see every step.
Show every step of every turn, with tool arguments, timings and each turn's model, tokens and cost.
gcode.chat.detail.description: How much of each turn the chat shows. The answer, the files a turn changed, and anything waiting on you show either way.

gcode.chat.bahtPerUsd.description: Baht to one US dollar, for the cost the composer shows while a turn runs. The tooltip gives the cost in US dollars.

gcode.tasks.osNotifications.description: Also show a macOS notification when a task finishes, fails or needs your answer while the VS Code window is not in front. Geno always shows its own notification inside VS Code.

enumDescriptions: Resume by itself when the provider's limit resets within 15 minutes. A longer wait holds until you choose Retry now.
Resume by itself whenever the limit resets, however long that is. Unattended use like this can break the interactive-use rule of a plan such as Model Studio's Coding Plan.
Never resume by itself after a limit. The turn waits until you choose Retry now or Stop.
gcode.resume.afterLimit.markdownDescription: When the provider rate-limits a turn, whether Geno sends the call again by itself once the limit resets. A turn that loses the network always resumes by itself. A change applies to the turns that start after it.

enumDescriptions: Save Geno's edits as they are made, with nothing to keep. Each turn that changed files ends in one line with Undo, which puts back every file as it was before the turn.
Put each of Geno's edits under review: Keep and Undo on every hunk, in the editor and in the chat.
gcode.review.mode.description: How you review the edits Geno has made. Approval modes (Ask, Auto, Plan) decide what Geno may do; this decides what happens after.

gcode.wake.auto.markdownDescription: Let a turn end while the background work it started still runs, and start a turn by itself when that work reports: a background subagent's report, a background command's end, a `monitor` match or a `schedule_wakeup`. It never starts one while you type, while a card waits for you, or while a turn runs, and pauses after 12 such turns in an hour. Off, a turn waits for its background subagents, and the rest waits for your next message. A change applies to the turns that start after it.

gcode.sandbox.allowedDomains.markdownDescription: More hosts the commands Geno runs may reach from the sandbox, such as `crates.io` or `*.example.com`. They add to the package hosts that `#gcode.sandbox.packageHosts#` opens. The list applies to every workspace, since the sandbox keeps one per engine, and a change restarts the engine. Web fetches and the browser follow the workspace's `WebFetch(domain:...)` and `Browser(domain:...)` rules instead.

gcode.sandbox.packageHosts.markdownDescription: Let the commands Geno runs reach the npm, Yarn and PyPI registries and GitHub (`registry.npmjs.org`, `registry.yarnpkg.com`, `pypi.org`, `files.pythonhosted.org`, `github.com`, `codeload.github.com`, `objects.githubusercontent.com`, `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`, `raw.githubusercontent.com`), so `npm install`, `pnpm add`, `yarn add`, `pip install` and `git clone` work. An install still asks in Ask mode and goes to the classifier in Auto. Off, the sandbox reaches only localhost and the hosts in `#gcode.sandbox.allowedDomains#`. A change restarts the engine.

gcode.additionalDirectories.markdownDescription: Folders beyond the workspace that Geno may read without asking, as Claude Code's `additionalDirectories`, such as `../shared` in a monorepo. A relative path starts at the workspace and `~/` at your home. A folder is read-only; write `{ "path": "../shared", "writable": true }` to let edits and commands write there too. Credentials files such as `.env` still ask. A workspace's value counts only in a trusted workspace, and a change restarts the engine. `additionalDirectories` in `.claude/settings.json` adds read-only folders too.

gcode.pages.folder.markdownDescription: The folder, inside the first workspace folder, where **Save as page** writes a widget or an answer as one standalone HTML file. A path that is absolute or leaves the workspace falls back to `geno-pages`.

gcode.ui.showChanges.description: Show Geno's Changes view under the chat. Off by default, since Source Control lists the same files; the chat's changes card and the editor's Keep and Undo lenses review edits either way.

gcode.tab.enabled.description: Show ghost-text completions from the local FIM model.

gcode.tab.endpoint.description: Base URL of the llama-server that serves Tab completions.

gcode.tab.modelPath.description: The GGUF file the Tab model server loads. Empty uses ~/.g-code/models/qwen2.5-coder-1.5b-q8_0.gguf. When Tab is on and nothing answers at gcode.tab.endpoint, Geno starts llama-server with it, and stops it when VS Code closes.

gcode.tab.debounceMs.description: Milliseconds to wait after the last keystroke before asking the model.

gcode.tab.nextEdit.description: Predict the next edit from recent edits with the local Zeta model, shown as inline edits. Needs VS Code Insiders with the inlineCompletionsAdditions proposal. Off by default because Zeta misses the latency bar on this Mac (docs/e9-e10-e11.md).

gcode.tab.nextEditEndpoint.description: Base URL of the llama-server that serves next-edit predictions (scripts/next-edit-server.sh).
